newsitem.title: GERMANY: West German preliminary inflation falls in March.
newsitem.headline: West German preliminary inflation falls in March.

text.p: Consumer prices in western Germany fell 0.1 percent in March from the previous month and were up 1.6 percent from the same month a year earlier, the Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday.

The figures are preliminary based on a survey of west Germany's four most populous states. Final March inflation data for all of Germany and the former west and east German regions will be released in around 10 days.
West German inflation rose 0.3 percent in February from the month before and was up 1.7 percent from the same month a year ago.

The March data were in line with economists's expectations and confirmed the view that the strong price increases in January and February did not set a trend for year. Falling prices for heating oil, package holidays and seasonal foods were largely behind the fall in the consumer price index in monthly comparison.

Economists polled earlier this week said they were unconcerned about German inflation, which has been at low levels for a long time, despite rising import prices fuelled by the recent increase in the strength of the dollar.

As a result of the favourable price climate, most economists do not expect the Bundesbank to change interest rates this year. But the central bank is also not expected to lower rates, but rather seek to keep rates at low levels for as long as possible.
